index.title: Technical labs
index.heading: Technical labs
index.description: Browser techniques that have no natural home in customer management, kept isolated from it on purpose.

unknown.heading: Unknown lab
unknown.body: There is no lab with that name
unknown.hint: The address may contain a typo, or the lab may have been renamed.

apiConnectivity.title: API connectivity
apiConnectivity.heading: API connectivity
apiConnectivity.description: Proves the plumbing end to end: the development proxy, the runtime-configured base URL, the HTTP interceptors, and validation of the response against the contract.

status.checking: Checking the connection to the API...
status.unavailable: The mock API is not reachable. Run it with: npm run start:api

browserStorage.title: Browser storage
browserStorage.description: localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB: what each holds, what each survives, and how other tabs hear about a change.
browserStorage.heading: Browser storage
browserStorage.unsupported: This browser does not offer it here - storage may be blocked for this site.
browserStorage.failed: The browser refused the storage operation. Storage may be full or blocked for this site.

webStorage.heading: localStorage and sessionStorage
webStorage.description: Save a value to each, then reload the page, open a new tab, or close and reopen this one: localStorage survives all three and is shared; sessionStorage survives only the reload.

events.heading: Storage events from other tabs
events.description: Open this page in a second tab and save to localStorage there. The browser tells this tab - and never the tab that wrote.

indexedDb.heading: IndexedDB
indexedDb.description: A database in the browser: structured records, written in transactions, without blocking the page. Notes survive reloads and restarts.
indexedDb.estimate: This site uses about {{usage}} KB of a {{quota}} MB quota.
indexedDb.persisted: Storage is persistent: the browser will not evict it under pressure.
indexedDb.bestEffort: Storage is best-effort: the browser may evict it when the disk fills.

crossTab.title: Cross-tab communication
crossTab.description: BroadcastChannel and storage events between tabs of the same application, and where the application itself uses them.
crossTab.heading: Cross-tab communication
crossTab.lede: Open this page in a second tab to see messages and changes arrive. This tab is {{id}}.

broadcast.heading: BroadcastChannel
broadcast.description: A message posted here reaches every other open tab of this application - not this one, and not a tab opened later.

storage.heading: Storage events
storage.description: The counter lives in localStorage. Incrementing it in any tab updates every other tab - the browser announces the change; nothing is sent.

application.heading: In the application
application.description: Four places the application itself coordinates tabs, outside this lab:
application.customers: A customer created, changed or deleted in one tab is announced in the others, which refresh what they show.
application.signOut: Signing out in one tab signs out every tab.
application.refresh: Two tabs never renew the session at the same instant: the refresh runs under a Web Lock.
application.theme: A theme chosen in one tab applies in the others, through the storage event.

offline.title: Offline and connectivity
offline.description: Detecting the network, a read-only list that survives losing it, and refreshing when it returns.
offline.heading: Offline and connectivity
offline.lede: One limited offline scenario: a read-only list of customers kept in IndexedDB. The rest of the application needs a network, and says so when there is none.

connectivity.heading: Connectivity
connectivity.description: What the browser reports. Offline is certain; online only means a network interface is up, not that the server answers.

directory.heading: Read-only customer list
directory.description: Fetched from the server while online and saved on this device; shown from the saved copy when the server cannot be reached.
directory.fromSaved: Saved copy from {{at}}. Read-only - it may be out of date.
directory.nothing: Nothing to show: the server cannot be reached and no copy has been saved on this device.
directory.name: Name

limits.heading: What this is not
limits.description: Changes are not queued, nothing is synchronised in the background, and pages you have not opened are not available offline. The saved copy belongs to the signed-in user and is deleted when the session ends in this tab. docs/offline.md has the details.

rendering.title: Rendering
rendering.description: The same page served five ways - client-rendered, server-rendered, prerendered, and prerendered with hydration switched off or deferred - and measured against each other.
rendering.heading: Rendering modes
rendering.lede: Five specimens of one page. Only how each is rendered differs, so any difference in the numbers is a difference in rendering.

specimens.heading: Specimens
specimens.description: Each link is a full page load from the server, not a navigation inside this application.
specimens.hydration: What the browser does with it

sources.client: Nowhere - an empty shell, rendered in the browser

hydrations.destructive: Throws the catalogue away and re-renders it
hydrations.incremental: Hydrates the catalogue when it scrolls into view

thisPage.heading: This page
thisPage.description: The application behind sign-in is client-rendered. These are the numbers for the load that produced this page; reload to measure again.

results.heading: Measured results
results.description: Controlled measurements - repeated runs, throttled network and CPU, medians - are produced by perf/measure-rendering.ts and recorded in docs/rendering.md.

client.name: Client-rendered (CSR)
client.summary: The server sends an empty document. Nothing appears until the JavaScript has downloaded, run and rendered the page.

server.name: Server-rendered (SSR)
server.summary: The server renders the page for this request. It appears as soon as the HTML arrives, and becomes interactive once hydrated.

prerender.name: Prerendered (SSG)
prerender.summary: The page was rendered once, at build time, and is served as a static file. It appears as soon as the HTML arrives, and becomes interactive once hydrated.

prerender-no-hydration.name: Prerendered, catalogue not hydrated
prerender-no-hydration.summary: Prerendered, but the catalogue opts out of hydration: the browser discards the server's markup for it and renders it again.

prerender-incremental.name: Prerendered, incremental hydration
prerender-incremental.summary: Prerendered, and the catalogue stays inert server markup until it scrolls into view - then it is hydrated.

specimen.title: Rendering specimen
specimen.heading: Specimen: {{mode}}
specimen.intro: Below the fold is a catalogue of 400 rows, each with a button - enough markup for hydration to cost something measurable.

performance.title: Performance
performance.heading: Performance
performance.description: Debouncing, throttling, memoization, virtual scrolling, image optimization and code splitting - each measured against its absence on a large dataset.
performance.lede: Every demo on this page works on the same {{count}} generated rows, and reports what it cost. Controlled numbers are in docs/performance.md.

rate.heading: Debouncing and throttling
rate.description: Every keystroke runs the immediate search over all rows; the debounced one waits for typing to pause. The pad counts pointer events against those a throttle lets through.
rate.searchHint: Scans all {{count}} rows by name or code
rate.padHint: Move the pointer across this area
rate.pointerHandled: Handled, throttled to one per {{ms}} ms

derived.heading: Memoization and derived state
derived.description: A summary of every row, derived by a template method and by a computed signal, while the component re-renders for an unrelated reason.
derived.result: {{strategy}}: summary recomputed {{recomputed}} times in {{renders}} renders, {{ms}} ms in total.

images.heading: Image optimization
images.description: Twelve pictures as the original upload in plain img tags, or through NgOptimizedImage: responsive WebP, lazy loading, reserved dimensions and a priority hint.

virtual.heading: Virtual scrolling
virtual.description: A plain list renders every row it is given; CDK virtual scrolling renders only the rows in view, whatever the size of the list.
virtual.deferred: This demo loads when it scrolls into view.

splitting.heading: Lazy loading and code splitting
splitting.description: Every page of the application is a lazy route, and the demo above is a deferred block with its own chunk. The bundle report in perf/bundle-report.ts says what the initial download holds and why; docs/performance.md has the numbers.

browserApis.title: Browser APIs
browserApis.heading: Browser APIs
browserApis.description: The URL, History, File, Clipboard, Permissions and Geolocation APIs - each feature-tested, and each with its refusals handled.

url.heading: URL API
url.description: Parse an address the way the browser does, relative to a base, with its query parameters decoded.
url.label: Address
url.invalid: Not an address the URL parser accepts.

history.heading: History API
history.description: Add history entries through the router - a query parameter that survives a reload, and navigation state that survives only back and forward.

file.heading: File API
file.description: Read a file you choose - its size, its first bytes, a SHA-256 digest - entirely in the page. Nothing is uploaded.
file.name: Name
file.failed: The file could not be read.

clipboard.heading: Clipboard API
clipboard.description: Writing is allowed from a click; reading asks for permission, because the clipboard may hold anything.

outcome.unsupported: The Clipboard API is not available here.

permissions.heading: Permissions API
permissions.description: Ask the browser what it would do - grant, refuse or prompt - without prompting the user.

geolocation.heading: Geolocation
geolocation.description: One position, when you ask. It is shown here and nowhere else.
geolocation.position: Latitude {{latitude}}, longitude {{longitude}}, accurate to about {{accuracy}} m.

failure.unavailable: The position could not be determined.
failure.timeout: Finding the position took too long.

workers.title: Workers
workers.heading: Web workers and service workers
workers.description: A Web Worker keeps heavy work off the thread that draws the page; a service worker sits between the page and the network.

worker.heading: Web Worker
worker.description: Count the primes below twenty million on the main thread, then in a worker, and compare how long the page stopped drawing frames.
worker.mainThread: Count primes below {{limit}} on the main thread
worker.worker: Count primes below {{limit}} in a worker
worker.result: {{where}}: {{count}} primes, {{total}} ms in total; the page's longest frame took {{frame}} ms.
worker.unsupported: This browser cannot start a Web Worker here.

serviceWorker.heading: Service worker
serviceWorker.description: Angular's service worker caches the application shell so it starts without a network. It runs only in production builds.
serviceWorker.disabledInDev: No - development builds do not register it

leaderElection.title: Leader election
leaderElection.description: Only one tab runs a periodic job; the others receive its result. A lease in localStorage, and its failure modes.
leaderElection.heading: Leader election
leaderElection.lede: Open this page in two or three tabs. One leads and polls the server; the others only listen. This is a learning experiment, not a production lock.

job.heading: The shared job
job.description: Every {{seconds}} seconds the leader asks the server how many customers exist, and tells the other tabs.
job.runHere: This tab has run the job {{count}} times.
